parts.title: My first summer job
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
On my sixteenth birthday, my uncle offered me a job in his restaurant for the summer. I was thrilled, until I saw what I had to do. My first week was spent in the kitchen, washing plates and cutting onions, and by Friday my hands were red and my eyes were sore. I was so disappointed that I thought about quitting.

Then one Saturday evening, one of the waiters did not turn up. My uncle looked at me and asked, 'Do you think you can carry plates?' I said yes before I could think. It was the busiest night of the week, and I was so nervous that I dropped a spoon in front of my first customers, a family with three small children. The children laughed, and then, to my relief, the mother laughed too.

After that, I got better quickly. I learned to remember orders without writing them down, and to smile even when somebody was rude. A cook called Marta taught me to say 'hot plate, please!' when I was carrying food through the busy kitchen, so that nobody walked into me. By the end of the summer, I was earning tips, and I had saved enough money to buy a second-hand guitar.

I have not decided what I want to do when I leave school. But I know that I do not want to sit behind a desk all day. Working with people can be tiring, but it is never boring.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel at the end of the first week?
questions.explanation: She was disappointed and thought about quitting after a week of washing plates and cutting onions.

questions.prompt: Why did she carry plates on Saturday evening?
options: A waiter had not come to work.
Her uncle wanted to test her.
She asked for a better job.
questions.explanation: One of the waiters did not turn up and her uncle asked her to help.

questions.prompt: What happened when she dropped the spoon?
options: The customers were very angry with her.
The family laughed in a friendly way.
Her uncle sent her home for the evening.
questions.explanation: The children laughed and then the mother laughed too, to her relief.

questions.prompt: What did Marta teach her?
options: To cook some very simple meals
To warn people about hot food
questions.explanation: Marta taught her to say 'hot plate, please!' so nobody walked into her.

questions.prompt: What does she say about her future?
options: She will become a cook one day.
She plans to study music at college.
She wants to work with people.
questions.explanation: She does not want to sit behind a desk all day and says working with people is never boring.

parts.title: The baker who starts at three
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
At three o'clock in the morning, when most of the town is asleep, Jorge is already at work. He is a baker, and he has the strangest timetable of anyone he knows. [1] His friends call him 'the owl', but he says that he would not change it for anything.

The first job is to prepare the dough, which has to rest for several hours. [2] Then the ovens must be heated, and the loaves are shaped by hand, one at a time. By six o'clock, the bakery smells wonderful.

The shop opens at seven, and by then a line of customers is waiting outside. Some of them have been buying bread from him for thirty years. [3] "I know exactly who likes their bread well baked and who prefers it soft," he says.

However, the job also has its problems. He sleeps in the afternoon, which means that he often misses family events. [4] In winter, the walk to work in the dark is cold and lonely.

Jorge hopes that his daughter will take over the bakery one day. [5] "She helped me last Christmas," he says proudly, "and she did not complain once, even though she had to get up at two."
sentences: He finishes his work when others are just beginning theirs.
In the meantime, he mixes the ingredients for the cakes.
Another problem is that he has very little time to relax in the evenings.
He is not sure that she wants to, but she has shown some interest.
He remembers most of them by name.
Bread was first baked in ovens made of clay.

gaps.explanation: "The strangest timetable" is explained by sentence A: he starts when others are asleep and finishes when they begin; the next sentence is about his nickname.
The dough must rest for hours; "In the meantime" says what he does while waiting, and then "the ovens must be heated".
Customers have bought bread for thirty years; "He remembers most of them by name" leads to what he knows about their preferences.
He misses family events; "Another problem" adds to the list, and the next sentence gives winter as a further problem.
He hopes his daughter will take over; he is not sure she wants to, but she has shown interest, and the next sentence describes how she helped.

parts.title: Writing a good CV
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: A CV is a short document that tells an employer about you. It should be clear and easy to [1], so use short sentences and a simple layout. Start with your name and contact details, and then list your education, beginning with the most [2] school or college. If you have no work experience, write about activities that show your skills, such as babysitting or helping at a club. Always check your CV carefully for spelling [3]. Many employers will not even read a CV that contains errors. [4] you have finished, ask a friend or a teacher to read it. Be honest about what you can do, because you may [5] to prove it in an interview. Finally, send your CV with a short letter explaining why you would like [6] job.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: A CV should be easy to read.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: You list education starting with the most recent school or college.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: Employers do not like spelling mistakes; the next sentence says they do not read CVs with errors.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: "When you have finished" says the time to ask a friend to read it.

questions.prompt: Gap 5

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: "Why you would like this job" refers to the job that you are applying for.

parts.title: A job application
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Mr Rossi,
I am writing [1] apply for the job of waiter at your café, which I saw advertised in the window. I am sixteen years old, and I [2] looking for a weekend job. I have [3] experience, but I am a quick learner, and I enjoy meeting people. At school, I was a member of the drama club, [4] has helped me to feel confident. I am free every Saturday and Sunday [5] the whole summer. I enclose my CV, and I look forward [6] hearing from you.
Yours sincerely,
Riley Hart

gaps.explanation: "I am writing to apply" gives the purpose of the letter.
The present continuous "am looking" needs the verb be.
"No experience, but a quick learner" shows the contrast.
"Which" refers to the whole fact of being in the drama club.
"For the whole summer" gives the length of time.

parts.title: A manager welcomes new staff
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Hillcrest Garden Centre. I'm Aurelia, the manager. Before you begin your first day, I want to explain a few important things. Work starts at half past eight, and we finish at five. You will have a lunch break of thirty minutes and two short breaks of ten minutes. Everyone must wear the green uniform, and a name badge, so that customers know who you are. If you are not sure about something, ask Sam, who works in the plant section and has been here for twenty years. Please remember that safety comes first: always wear gloves when you handle the heavy bags of soil. In case of a fire, the exit is at the back of the shop, next to the café. Finally, no mobile phones are allowed on the shop floor.

parts.title: An interview with a paramedic
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wolfgang, you are a paramedic. How did you come to choose this job?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: When I was twelve, my grandfather had a heart attack. The paramedic who arrived was so calm and kind that I decided right then that I wanted to be like her.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does a normal shift look like?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: There is no such thing as normal. One day, we might help somebody who has fallen off a ladder, and the next, we might be called to a car accident. Most shifts last twelve hours, and we are often too busy to sit down.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the most important quality for the job?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: Staying calm. When people are frightened, they look to you for help. If you panic, they panic. So I speak slowly and clearly, and I always explain what I am doing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Is the work stressful?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: Yes, at times. We see difficult things. That's why we always talk to our colleagues afterwards. A cup of tea and a chat can help more than people think.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the best part of the job?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: Hearing that somebody we helped has recovered. Last year, a woman sent a card to say that her baby, who was born in our ambulance, had just started school.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you say to a young person thinking about this career?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: Get some first-aid training, even a basic course. And try volunteering with a first-aid group. It will show you whether this is really the right job for you.

questions.prompt: Why did Wolfgang decide to become a paramedic?

He wanted to drive very fast in traffic.
questions.explanation: A calm and kind paramedic came when his grandfather had a heart attack and he wanted to be like her.

questions.explanation: He says there is no normal shift, and most last twelve hours with little time to sit.

questions.prompt: What does he think is the most important quality?
questions.explanation: He says the most important thing is to stay calm so that frightened people do not panic.

questions.prompt: How do paramedics deal with stress?
